nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What products are formed as per Equations [6] through [14] mentioned in the text?
nodes.answer: NaAIO2 is formed in Equations [6] through [7], [10] through [12], and [14], while Al4C3 is formed in Equations [13] and [14].

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What was the post-treatment carbon purity achieved after the proposed treatment of SPL?
nodes.answer: The post-treatment carbon purity achieved was up to 98 wt pct after treating 519 kg of SPL for four hours.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What was the yield percentage of the final product obtained?
nodes.answer: The yield percentage of the final product obtained was 70%.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the carbon content of the carbonaceous by-product derived from SPL?
nodes.answer: The carbon content of the carbonaceous by-product is about 30-40 wt pct.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How has the carbonaceous by-product been utilized in the construction industry?
nodes.answer: It has been used as construction material for Rio Tinto's bauxite residue dams and in the cement industry.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What potential energy source does the carbon-rich part of the by-product represent when its carbon content reaches 80-85 pct?
nodes.answer: The carbon-rich part can be used as an energy source.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_006
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How does the utilization of the first cut SPL in carbon products like anodes compare to its use as fuel?
nodes.answer: Utilizing the first cut SPL in products like anodes approaches reuse without down-cycling, as over 80 pct of the potential energy in carbon anodes is utilized for producing valuable products like aluminum, unlike when carbon is used as fuel which results in CO2 emissions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_007
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is noted about iodine doping in relation to carbon materials?
nodes.answer: Iodine doping is beginning to be considered for applications, although there is still limited research on its effects in porous carbon structures.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_008
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What process is used to synthesize iodine@S-doped SPAC?
nodes.answer: The synthesis of iodine@S-doped SPAC is achieved through a series of pyrolysis and hydrothermal processes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is glucose considered a valuable product, and what are some of its important applications?
nodes.answer: Glucose is valuable as it serves as the raw material for various economic productions like bioethanol, lactic acid, sorbitol, ethylene glycol, and terephthalic acid.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_010
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What kind of valuable chemicals do halophilic bacteria produce for pharmaceutical and medical applications?
nodes.answer: Halophilic bacteria produce valuable chemicals such as osmolytes (ectoine, hydroxyectoine), pigments, amino acids (proline), and natural coenzymes (ubiquinone).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_011
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the role of Dicranopteris pedata in the study mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Dicranopteris pedata is used as a rare earth elements (REEs) hyperaccumulator to fabricate REEs-rich carbonisation materials for remediation purposes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Carbon capture and storage|Carbon capture and utilization (ccu)_qna_012
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is a proposed strategy for treating hyperaccumulator biomass after soil REE extraction?
nodes.answer: Dicranopteris pedata is proposed to be a precursor to one-step fabrication of REEs-enriched carbonisation materials (REEs/C).
